sections.h2: Where do deeds get recorded in Craven County, NC?
sections.html:
Deeds for Craven County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds office, 226 Pollock Street, New Bern, NC 28560. The office's phone line is 252-636-6617.

The county's own page says the register is one of three county-wide elected offices created under North Carolina law. It records, indexes and preserves deeds, deeds of trust, plats, maps and other instruments affecting property, and it also keeps vital records, issues marriage licenses and records assumed business names and military discharges. Its holdings reach back more than three centuries, which matters in a county as old as this one when a title search turns up an early family tract.

For a seller, the practical rule is the cutoff. The register's notary page states that the office stops recording at 4:30 p.m. and will not swear in notaries after that time either. A closing that finishes at 4:45 p.m. will likely be recorded the next business day.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Craven County?
sections.html:
An ordinary deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page after that. The county's fee page lists a deed of trust at $64 for the first 35 pages, again with $4 for each additional page.

Real estate recording charges listed by the Craven County Register of Deeds

The fee schedule is labeled as of October 1, 2016, and the office asks buyers and sellers to call before relying on payment types other than cash, check or card. Online vital-record orders through the county's vendor add a $3.50 convenience fee, but that does not apply to a real estate recording.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax in Craven County?
sections.html:
The seller does. State law puts the duty on the transferor, who pays the register before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each $500 of price or value (G.S. 105-228.30). The register's fee page repeats the rate in the same words.

  • The tax counts any fraction of $500 as a full $500 unit.
  • Half the proceeds go to the county general fund and half to the state.
  • The amount follows the deed's stated consideration or value, so the figure belongs on the seller's side of the settlement statement.

Your closing attorney will compute the exact dollars. This page prints rates only, and the figure on your own deed may differ if the price is not the full value of what changes hands.

sections.h2: How do I record electronically or search Craven County records?
sections.html:
The register's Real Estate page lists three tools: an e-recording partner page, a public records search, and a page on UCC filings. Those links sit beside an online search of the public records and a Recordation Notification service, which the office promotes on every page of its site.

E-recording suits lenders and closing offices that send many documents. If you are a private seller and your closing is handled by an attorney, you will rarely file anything yourself. If you do file by mail, the UCC page instructs that checks be made payable to Register of Deeds at the Pollock Street address.

  • Use the online records search to pull your vesting deed and confirm the legal description.
  • Look for a deed of trust that has no matching satisfaction before you list.
  • Sign up for the recordation notification if you want a message when a document is filed against your name.

sections.h2: What does registration do to a seller's title in Craven County?
sections.html:
Registration fixes priority. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value, and later claims rank by the time each was registered.

That is the reason sellers ask for the recording confirmation after funding. A release of an old mortgage works the same way, and since satisfactions cost nothing to record here, there is no excuse for a paid-off loan to linger on the index.

North Carolina's contract for deed law, Chapter 47H, adds a recording duty of its own. The seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days, the buyer can cancel until midnight of the third business day, and a forfeiture needs a written notice that gives at least 30 days to cure. If you consider financing a buyer yourself, start with that chapter.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Craven County homes?
sections.html:
Craven County is a mid-sized, growing market. The Census Bureau estimates 105,025 residents for July 2025, up from 100,720 at the 2020 census, and counts 50,334 housing units across 706.57 square miles of land.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $231,600 (2020-2024).
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 68.4%.
  • Median household income: $65,873 in 2024 dollars.
  • Median gross rent: $1,110.
  • Residents 65 and older: 24.2%.
  • Veterans: 10,968.
  • Building permits in 2025: 553.

Population density runs about 142.5 people per square mile, well above the rural counties to the west, and the town list on the county site (Bridgeton, Cove City, Dover, Havelock, New Bern, River Bend, Trent Woods and Vanceboro) shows how the housing stock spreads across river towns and small crossroads communities.

sections.h2: How does a Craven County seller deal with flood and tax matters at the register's office?
sections.html:
The county's planning department improved its Community Rating System class from 8 to 7, and the county says owners in unincorporated areas now receive a 15% discount on flood insurance premiums, up from 10%. That is a selling point if your home sits near the Neuse or Trent rivers, and the buyer's insurance agent can confirm what applies to a given address.

Tax bills are separate from the register. County property tax is due September 1, with the last day to pay without interest on January 5, and the county's FY 2026-2027 budget kept the rate at 44.48 cents per $100 of assessed value. Ask the Tax Collection Division, at 252-636-6605, for a payoff figure before closing so the bill is cleared when the deed is recorded.

If the home has gone to tax foreclosure, the register is only the place the final deed is filed. The county's foreclosure page lists properties for sale and gives the tax collection email for questions.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Craven County property?
faqs.a: Record it at the Craven County Register of Deeds, 226 Pollock Street in New Bern. The office stops recording at 4:30 p.m., so a deed that arrives later is normally filed the next business day.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Craven County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page, per the county fee page. A deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Craven County?
faqs.a: No. The county fee schedule lists a satisfaction of deed of trust at no charge, so a paid-off loan can be cleared from the index for free.

faqs.q: Who pays excise tax on a Craven County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the register before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1 per $500 of consideration, counting any part of $500 as a full unit.

faqs.q: Can I search Craven County deeds without visiting the office?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers an online public records search and a recordation notification service, and e-recording is available through partner vendors listed on the Real Estate page.
